hero.name: Danil Zablotsky
hero.statement: I design interfaces and build them into working products on iOS, Android and the web myself.

story.title: My story
story.lead: From a menu for a game to a product of my own: how I became a design engineer.

omsk.title: It started with a menu for a game
omsk.school: A maths and physics class, plus programming lessons: we wrote websites right in Notepad, in plain HTML, CSS and JS. From the seventh grade I lived in Photoshop, then found Illustrator, and in the eleventh, Figma.
omsk.game: In it I built a menu for a game I played all the time and posted it in the game's groups. People asked how to install it. It reached the developers: they offered me work, then opened my file and stopped answering.
omsk.quote: Over a hundred frames. Not one component.
omsk.after: I was furious at the time. Now I understand them.
omsk.menus: The Figma file of the game menu: dozens of nearly identical screens

university.title: Maths first
university.choice: I wanted to study product design, but a teacher talked me out of it: get your maths up first. So I ended up at Omsk State University, in applied mathematics and computer science.
university.roles: Programming came easily and I enjoyed it, but in group projects I still ended up as the designer.
university.quote: It's a pain to check my own class schedule.
university.idea: Some universities had apps for that. From 2023 Maxim, a classmate of mine, and I kept talking about building one for ours, and kept putting it off: the idea felt too big.

build.title: VCourse
build.start: In our third year we were given a semester to build a product of our own, and neural networks had just grown up enough. We went for it. I took product design and the front end, Maxim the back end and DevOps.
build.learn: I had no experience in mobile development at all. The first semester went on Swift, SwiftUI, Xcode and Apple's guidelines.
build.quote: By the end of the semester my own app was on my phone.
build.polish: The next semester and the summer went on polish. The app was rewritten from scratch several times: I wanted it perfect.
build.layers: The VCourse profile screen in Xcode's view debugger, pulled apart into layers
build.update: A lock screen notification: VCourse updated to version 0.1.0
build.icon: Icon Composer with an icon of two circles on blue

launch.title: Launch
launch.post: We agreed with the university on a post in its Telegram channel. The post went out, and we sat refreshing the pages, watching the numbers.
launch.stageCaption: Presenting VCourse to first-years, as a fourth-year
launch.rankLabel: rank among education apps on the Russian App Store at launch
launch.chartSummary: 632 downloads in the first three days, 411 of them on 2 September.

fork.title: The fork
fork.question: In the semester after the launch came Android and the website, and five more colleges and universities joined. It all worked, and the question came up: what next? We couldn't keep growing it seriously and earn nothing from it.
fork.quote: Ads in the app, or a service for universities.
fork.answer: We really didn't want ads. We took the second road: our own service for building timetables, with the apps as a pleasant extra for students and teachers. We started talking to the people who make the timetables and took apart how it's really done.
fork.score: A week as a musical score: tangled lines fall into straight rows, with strokes for classes on them

night.title: One night
night.letter: My bachelor's was ending and I was looking at master's programmes in Omsk. One night a newsletter from Central University arrived: a programme in Human Experience Design. In essence, the product design I had wanted to study after school.
night.need: They wanted a portfolio. I had none.
night.quote: I decided not to sleep until I had built something worth sending.
night.wait: The application went out. Then a call, and several weeks of silence.
night.grant: And then a letter: the largest grant they give.

rent.quote: …and now I had to pay for a flat somehow

moscow.title: Ten prompts
moscow.study: At the end of the summer I moved and started my master's at Central University.
moscow.job: Alongside it I worked in a team: several iOS app designs a week, plus their ASO. Doing that by hand would have driven me mad.
moscow.agents: I tried agents in Figma. That took a whole pipeline, and it worked.
moscow.quote: The tool took the routine. The decisions stayed with me.
moscow.prompts: I won’t claim a complete app, with icons and an App Store page, came out of one prompt. I will claim it came out of ten thoughtful, consecutive ones.

now.title: A product and a master's
now.quote: I want to make products where design and code are one job.

open.name: Open to a conversation
open.text: If you need someone who designs and takes it all the way to code, write to me.

pora.name: Pora na paru
pora.label: My own product · since 2024
pora.text: A schedule service for universities and apps for students. One and the same lesson lives in the browser, on the iPhone and on Android, and I write all three clients myself.

stage.value: alpha test on iOS and Android, the web is open

clients.value: iOS, Android and the web since 2 June 2026

pora.note: The frames are the product's real screens on made-up data.

web.title: The week in a browser
web.text: The week of any group, teacher or room by a link, nothing to install. Open since 16 October 2026.
web.alt: The schedule in a browser: a group's week, Monday, the first lesson going on.

ios.title: The lesson on the lock screen
ios.text: On the iPhone the lesson going on holds itself in a Live Activity and the Dynamic Island, and turns into the break and the end of the day. The store build has been with testers in TestFlight since 27 September 2026.
ios.alt: The iPhone's lock screen with the Live Activity of the lesson going on.

android.title: The same lesson on Android
android.text: By Android's rules: the home holds favourite groups and teachers, the lesson going on and notes for lessons, and the lesson is in a widget too. The colours of Material 3 Expressive. In a closed test on Google Play since 30 September 2026.
android.alt: The Android app's home: favourites, the lesson going on and notes for lessons.

editor.title: Publishing without clashes
editor.text: An editor for the academic office: a teacher booked for two lessons at once lights up before publishing, and a moved lesson reaches every app at once. The editor is being designed.
editor.conflict: Clash: Ivanov D.N. in two lessons at once

flow.name: Flow
flow.label: Case · iOS app production line, 2026
flow.text: How I fitted agents to production-line design: a terminal and a Markdown knowledge base carried a task from the brief to finished screens. It was a solution for one type of work, not my usual process.
flow.note: The task in the demo is made up.

brief.title: Brief
brief.text: The task became a short brief and a board of six style directions.
brief.me: I picked the style and answered questions
brief.tool: A brief in ten minutes, visual research, a style board
brief.hint: Pick a direction for me: the screens ahead will take its colours.

research.title: Research
research.text: References from real apps, a breakdown of patterns and a map of screens.
research.me: Review, then “go”: stage 2 waited for my word
research.tool: Research, screen map, tokens, wireframes, audit

screens.title: Screens
screens.text: A wireframe became a screen in place: the same frames on the same coordinates.
screens.me: I reviewed the key screens at the stop
screens.tool: Components, onboarding, paywall, main feature, other branches

handoff.title: Handoff
handoff.text: One run gave a file that could go to development.
handoff.me: I walked the file, fixed it or sent it back
handoff.tool: Prototype, cover, 28 icons, two store sets, assets

rule.title: A note became a rule
rule.text: A note was not fixed once. Here is the real history of one dot of this graph.

base.title: Back to the base

projects.name: Projects
projects.label: Besides the product
projects.text: Two projects of my own: this site and everything I do in LaTeX. On their page they lie on a board, like mockups in an editor.
projects.themes: Every page declares its theme: colours, typefaces and the look of controls. Two modes make eight combinations. A component reads tokens and knows nothing of themes.
projects.releases: The thesis came out in releases, like a program. Each release is a dated tag: GitHub Actions builds the PDF in a container with TeX Live and attaches it to the release.
